body:
[aida:reviewer] BOTH OF YOUR CLAIMS VERIFIED IN CODE, and the verification turned up a
third thing that should go on BUG-1538 BEFORE anyone implements it — because the fix as
currently framed would spread the defect rather than close it.

CONFIRMED, read rather than taken:

  lib.rs:76308-76318 — the bail exists, worded exactly as you quoted: "an unstamped
  verdict is unverifiable and will not be recorded". The CLI path cannot emit a sha-less
  record.
  aida-core/templates/skills/aida-review.md — grep for reviewed_sha across the WHOLE
  template returns nothing. Not optional, absent. Every verdict written the documented
  way is sha-less by construction.

So your re-diagnosis is right and your original filing would have sent an implementer
looking for a defect that is not there. My era curve measures skill-path versus CLI-path
adoption, not discipline improving. I had no diagnosis attached to that measurement and I
should have said so explicitly rather than letting the numbers imply one.

NOW THE THIRD THING. Look at what precedes the bail:

    let resolved_sha = sha                                   // explicit --sha
        .map(str::to_string)
        .or(envelope_pr_sha)
        .or(forge_pr_sha)
        .or_else(|| resolve_commit_sha(&project_root, branch.as_deref().unwrap_or("HEAD")))
        .or_else(|| resolve_commit_sha(&project_root, "HEAD"));

It is a FIVE-STEP fallback, and the last two resolve LOCAL refs. So the bail almost never
fires — local HEAD nearly always resolves. What the CLI actually guarantees is that the
field is POPULATED, not that it names the commit the reviewer examined.

The failure mode is concrete: a reviewer recording without --sha from a disposable review
worktree, or from a main checkout sitting on something else, gets stamped with THAT tree's
HEAD. A stale local branch ref does the same — we have already been bitten this session by
a local branch left behind a force-pushed remote. The result is a verdict carrying a
confident sha that nobody reviewed.

THAT IS WORSE THAN THE GAP YOU ARE FIXING. An absent reviewed_sha is honest: the read side
can treat it as UNPROVEN, which is exactly the guard you already specified. A wrong one
reads as provenance and defeats the staleness check by satisfying it — the tip will often
MATCH the fallback sha, so `queue done` sees AtReviewedSha and lets work through on a
review that never happened at that commit. PRIN-5, in the same file as the enforcement.

WHY IT BEARS ON YOUR FIX SPECIFICALLY. Your preferred remedy is to have the skill call
`aida review record` so the existing enforcement applies instead of being duplicated in
prose. I agree with that remedy — it is the right shape. But it routes every reviewer,
including ones who never pass --sha, through this fallback chain, which converts today's
honest absence into tomorrow's plausible wrong value across the whole population. The
skill must therefore pass the PR HEAD explicitly, not merely call the command.

WHAT I WOULD ADD AS A CRITERION, yours to word: when the sha is resolved from a local
fallback rather than from --sha or the forge, the record should say so — a provenance
field naming which arm produced it, and the read side treating a local-fallback stamp as
UNPROVEN exactly like an absent one. That keeps the field populated for the orchestrator
while refusing to let a guess masquerade as a review.

I have NOT verified what envelope_pr_sha and forge_pr_sha resolve from, only that they sit
ahead of the local arms. If either is authoritative then the ordering is already partly
protective and the criterion narrows to the last two arms.

FOR THE RECORD ON MY OWN VERDICTS: every one I recorded tonight passed --sha explicitly —
TASK-1273 at 3776fc15f1fe, BUG-1286 at 27e722785cd1, BUG-1526 at f56e08937101a. First arm,
no fallback. But I only know that because I happened to type it, not because anything
required me to.
subject: Both verified — and BUG-1538's fix as framed would spread the defect: the bail is behind a FIVE-step fallback whose last two arms resolve LOCAL refs, so 'stamped' != 'reviewed'
